purpose: Broaden evaluation beyond the first four calibration contracts. Selection and tasks precede import and analysis; unfamiliar means not previously evaluated or tuned in this project. Verified metadata is scoring ground truth, never a reconstruction input. Keep failures and timeouts in the report.

contracts.expected_family: Wrapped native currency with token accounting and ETH withdrawals
inspection_tasks: Explain deposit and withdrawal accounting, including fallback deposits
Identify the ETH transfer, its failure behavior and authorization bounds
Explain finite versus unlimited allowances and the emitted events

contracts.expected_family: Name registry with ownership, operators and nested record storage
inspection_tasks: Explain authorization for changing records and subnode ownership
Identify resolver and TTL storage updates and emitted events
Explain operator approvals and calls to any legacy registry

contracts.expected_family: Enumerable NFT collection with dynamic metadata and mint administration
inspection_tasks: Identify transfer authorization and the safe-transfer receiver callback
Explain enumeration storage updates and dynamic metadata returns
Explain mint bounds, payment checks and administrative authority

contracts.expected_family: Multisignature wallet implementation with signatures, modules and arbitrary execution
inspection_tasks: Explain owner membership, threshold and signature validation paths
Identify transaction CALL versus DELEGATECALL and failure behavior
Explain module and guard authorization and their external interactions

comparison_requirements: Identical runtime hashes for each comparison and retained archived-response provenance
Detect duplicates against upstream bytecodes and the first calibration corpus
Run the pinned implementation before changes motivated by these contracts
Withhold verified ABI and source from reconstruction; record any independent signature dictionary
Retain missing selectors, failed analyses and timeouts rather than replacing cases
Separate coverage from behavioral correctness and inspection-task usefulness
Dedaub parity requires actual same-bytecode output and an explicit comparison
